ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A, D, B are on the same upper horizontal line segment, and D is between A and B; from D downward there is a vertical line segment CD, and there is a right-angle mark at D, indicating that CD is perpendicular to AB. In the figure, AD is labeled as 5, CD is labeled as 12, and the hypotenuse BC is labeled as 31.2. The large triangle is triangle ABC, and the small triangle is triangle CBD. Reasoning: From the figure, AD = 5, CD = 12, and AD ⟂ CD, so triangle ADC is a right triangle, AC = sqrt(5^2 + 12^2) = sqrt(169) = 13. According to the given similarity relation triangle ABC ∼ triangle CBD, the corresponding sides are AB ↔ CB, BC ↔ BD, AC ↔ CD. Using AC/CD = BC/BD, we get 13/12 = 31.2/BD, therefore BD = 31.2 × 12 / 13 = 28.8. Thus AB = AD + DB = 5 + 28.8 = 33.8. The perimeter of triangle ABC is AB + BC + AC = 33.8 + 31.2 + 13 = 78.

raw_record.question_text: Find the perimeter of $\triangle ABC$ if $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle CBD$, $AD=5$, $CD=12$, and $BC=31.2$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: A, D, B are collinear on the top segment, CD is perpendicular to AB, AD is the short top-left segment, and CD is the vertical segment down to C. Use the text-given similarity order \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle CBD\), so the corresponding sides are \(AB \leftrightarrow CB\), \(BC \leftrightarrow BD\), and \(AC \leftrightarrow CD\). From the image and text, \(AD=5\) and \(CD=12\), with a right angle at D, so \(AC=13\) by the Pythagorean theorem. Then use \(AC/CD = BC/BD\): \(13/12 = 31.2/BD\), giving \(BD=28.8\). Since \(AB=AD+DB=5+28.8=33.8\), the perimeter is \(AB+BC+AC=33.8+31.2+13=78\).
